newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DIARY - DUTCH POLITICAL AGENDA -- WEEK OF DEC 16.
newsitem.headline: DIARY - DUTCH POLITICAL AGENDA -- WEEK OF DEC 16.

text.p: Following are some of the main
issues scheduled for debate in the Dutch parliament this week:
DRUGS -- New rules determining extent to which police and
prosecutors may turn blind eye to sale and use of hashish and
marihuana will be debated on Thursday. Government plans to
reduce amount of soft drugs costumer is allowed to buy in
"coffeeshops" to five grams from 30.
BUDGET -- Parliament on Thursday debates Finance Minister's
end-of-year survey of government spending and revenues. Budget
deficit expected to amount to less than earlier projected 2.6
percent of GDP because of higher than expected tax receipts.
BOSNIA -- Continuing reconstruction and reconciliation
efforts in Bosnia to be debated with Foreign and Defence
Ministers on Thursday.
Other issues to be debated:
MONDAY:
- Evaluation of recent European Union summit in Dublin.
- Parliament to confirm plans to build high speed railway
track between Amsterdam and Antwerp.
TUESDAY:
- MPs and electrical goods industry representatives to
discuss increased recycling of electrical devices.
WEDNESDAY:
- Cleaning up of polluted river beds.
- Stimulation of genetics research and technology to improve
competitiveness of Dutch agriculture.
Reducing construction of houses in river flood plains.
- Setting of stricter rules for transport of livestock.
THURSDAY:
- Implementation of plan to reduce number of children per
class in primary education.
- Relaxation of labour laws to allow 12 hour workshifts and
other exceptions to labour laws in certain circumstances.
The Lower House last week discussed:
DUTCH EU PRESIDENCY -- Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said
tactic of ignoring Britain's "Eurosceptical" position on EU
issues until British elections might be suitable way to ease
negotiations during Dutch EU presidency beginning January 1.
DRUGS -- Parliament criticised government for jeopardising
liberal Dutch drugs policy due to "clumsy" negotiating stance in
preparatory talks on common European action against illegal
drugs trade. EU's joint action stopped short of forbidding Dutch
to maintain their odd-man-out liberal policy line on drugs.
